chapter.heading: Romans 11
The Remnant of Israel
chapter.v: I myself am an Israelite, a descendant of Abraham, a member of the tribe of Benjamin.
foreknew. Do you not know what the Scripture says of Elijah, how he appeals to God against Israel?
“Lord, they have killed your prophets, they have demolished your altars, and I alone am left, and they seek my life.”
“I have kept for myself seven thousand men who have not bowed the knee to Baal.”
a remnant, chosen by grace.
But if it is by grace, it is no longer on the basis of works; otherwise grace would no longer be grace.
were hardened,
down to this very day.”
a stumbling block and a retribution for them;
and bend their backs forever.”
salvation has come to the Gentiles, so as to make Israel jealous.
Now if their trespass means riches for the world, and if their failure means riches for the Gentiles, how much more will their full inclusion mean!
I am an apostle to the Gentiles, I magnify my ministry
thus save some of them.
the reconciliation of the world, what will their acceptance mean but life from the dead?
If the dough offered as firstfruits is holy, so is the whole lump, and if the root is holy, so are the branches.
although a wild olive shoot, were grafted in among the others and now share in the nourishing root of the olive tree,
do not be arrogant toward the branches. If you are, remember it is not you who support the root, but the root that supports you.
Then you will say, “Branches were broken off so that I might be grafted in.”
fear.
For if God did not spare the natural branches, neither will he spare you.
you too will be cut off.
even they, if they do not continue in their unbelief, will be grafted in, for God has the power to graft them in again.

For if you were cut from what is by nature a wild olive tree, and grafted, contrary to nature, into a cultivated olive tree, how much more will these, the natural branches, be grafted back into their own olive tree.
